note: The public fact/claim/unknown ledger. Every fact entry names the record its rendering is recomputed from and every surface that rendering must appear on verbatim; tools/ci/check_claims.py refuses a stale one. Corrections append and never overwrite: a correction retains the superseded text with a digest over it, and the checker refuses a commit that removes one the parent revision carried. Rendered to docs/public-claims.md and docs/public-claims.ar.md by `python tools/ci/check_claims.py --write`; edit this file and regenerate, never the views.
bound_statement: The gate refuses a merge, not an edit: the rewrite lands in a working tree before anything refuses it, and a clone taken from that tree carries the rewrite. It holds only where tools/ci/check_claims.py runs and is a required check -- a branch with checks disabled, a direct push to a repository without the workflow, or a fork are all outside it. Rewriting the revision the checker compares against, by force-push or by rebase, defeats the comparison; the per-entry history digest and this ledger's head_digest let anyone holding an earlier copy detect that, and prove nothing to anyone who does not hold one. Nothing here is anchored in a transparency log, notarized, or countersigned, so an entry's history is verifiable offline against a copy you already trust and against nothing else. And no status in this ledger is evidence about the world: fact means "recomputed from a named record in this repository", not "true".

claims.text: No netns, seccomp or firewall enforcement exists in this repository. rust/warrant/src/sandbox.rs derives a bubblewrap or firejail command line that carries --unshare-net or --net=none when a warrant grants no egress, and it launches nothing: that module emits a profile and its own header says it enforces nothing. A bound this project describes as contained is contained at settle time, which is Observed and not Enforced; a bound that holds only for traffic through the proxy is a chokepoint bound and what bypasses the proxy escapes it. Containment composes with an external sandbox and does not replace one.

falsifier.how: code under rust/ is found launching a confinement profile, or applying a network namespace, seccomp filter or firewall rule itself, at which point a stronger word than Observed becomes available for the bound it holds

corrections.reason: The published sentence is true and invites a reading that is not. rust/warrant/src/sandbox.rs derives a bubblewrap or firejail command line carrying --unshare-net or --net=none when a warrant grants no egress, and the falsifier as published asked whether a namespace is found being applied by code under rust/ -- so anyone grepping for the falsifier's own terms finds the two flags and cannot tell from the entry that nothing launches the profile. The replacement names the emitting module, so the grep resolves without reading the module, and sharpens the falsifier to launching rather than mentioning.

claims.text: tools/ci/check_claims.py refuses a commit that changes a published entry's status, text or falsifier without raising the version and appending a correction that retains what the parent revision published, and refuses one that removes or alters a retained correction. It establishes nothing about an entry the parent revision did not carry: a new entry may arrive at version 2 carrying a version 1 nobody can check, and a version that rises by more than one leaves the intermediate retained texts unattested.

falsifier.how: rewrite a published entry's text in evidence/claims.json, leave its version at what it was, run python tools/ci/check_claims.py --write and then python tools/ci/check_claims.py --parent-ref HEAD; an exit code of 0 falsifies this

corrections.reason: As published in commit 3c2baa9 this sentence named a refusal the checker did not perform. check_append_only compared versions and retained corrections and never compared the parent revision's text, so leaving the version at 1 and replacing the text passed the gate once --write had refreshed the head -- and a correction could retain a superseded_text that hashed to itself and to nothing anyone ever published. Both were found by running the gate against a hand-built rewrite rather than by reading the code, and both are refused as of this commit. This is the eight-incident defect of this repository, committed inside the artifact built to catch it. Backticks are stripped from this quotation of a README table cell; nothing else is changed.
corrections.superseded_text: tools/ci/check_claims.py refuses a commit that changes a published entry without retaining the previous text, and refuses one that removes a retained correction.
